extracted.intended_audience: government agency staff, researchers, and practitioners designing or running e-rulemaking / public comment platforms
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and running online e-rulemaking projects that maximize informed public discussion and meaningful comments on proposed federal rules. Focuses on site selection, outreach, facilitation, and comment-support practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on technology alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Using cool new technologies is not enough to draw people to visit a website and comment on proposed rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technology should be combined with deliberate design and outreach; a flashy site by itself will not generate informed participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target specific audiences affected by the rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiatives must be designed to target specific audiences affected by the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify stakeholder groups who are impacted by a proposal and tailor outreach, messaging, and content to reach them (especially those unlikely to be aware or to comment on their own).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select proposals carefully for discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rules are chosen carefully for discussion, focusing on proposals that could have a major effect on stakeholders who are not likely to be aware of the proposals and not likely to comment on their own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize rulemakings with clear, tangible stakes for identifiable groups. Example: DOT airline passenger rights generated >24,000 visits, while a proposal about onboard recorders drew only a few hundred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make outreach an essential part of the plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting up a website for public discussion is just the beginning; outreach has been crucial for making stakeholders aware and motivating participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social networks, blogs, and other tools to publicize discussions. Team members should actively visit related blogs and Facebook pages and post links directing people to the e-rulemaking site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help people analyze the proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: E-rulemaking projects should provide help in analyzing the proposed rule, since most people do not have time to read long Federal Register notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise outlines of key points, explain difficult details, and point to areas where the proposal might affect stakeholders so participants can be informed without reading full notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide guidance and facilitation for making effective comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide guidance for making effective comments; moderators can answer questions and clarify information and help participants move beyond anger to address pertinent issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use moderators to respond to questions, correct misunderstandings, and coach commenters toward focusing on substantive issues. Facilitators can transform emotional reactions into constructive, issue-focused comments.
